title: ALBERT factorized embedding plus domain Mirror views
hypothesis: A small domain Givens coordinate applied inside an ALBERT-style low-dimensional token embedding bottleneck can restore useful domain-specific functions for held-out token-domain pairs at lower actual bytes than domain adapters applied after the embedding projection.
physical_object: one shared 4D vocabulary embedding table and one shared 4D-to-16D projection
mirror_coordinate: one Givens angle per domain, applied in the 4D embedding bottleneck before the shared projection

model.data: Synthetic token-domain classification. A shared token latent is transformed by a domain-specific Givens rotation in the 4D bottleneck and projected to 16D before a shared classifier. A seed-locked 25% of token-domain pairs is held out while each token and domain remains represented in training.

controls: ALBERT-style hard-shared 4D embedding plus shared projection
domain FiLM after the shared projection
rank-2 domain LoRA adapter after the shared projection
Mirror domain angle inside the 4D bottleneck
development_gate_before_fresh: Both seeds: independent seen-pair accuracy >=0.80; Mirror seen-pair accuracy within 0.02 of the best non-independent control; Mirror held-out-pair accuracy >=0.05 absolute above ALBERT hard sharing; actual payload <=1.10x the smallest ALBERT/FiLM/LoRA control and <=0.50x independent embedding; count unique FP16 role embeddings; serialized-state CPU throughput >=0.90x the fastest shared control. Fresh remains sealed if any gate misses.
success_gate: All three fresh worlds pass held-out quality, bytes, uniqueness, runtime and exact replay, and Mirror improves the quality-byte frontier over hard sharing and domain adapters.
failure_gate: Any development seed misses a registered gate or an outside-embedding adapter matches the held-out transfer at comparable/lower bytes.

storage.authority: actual deterministic ZIP/NPY FP16 payload after reload
paid_objects: all FiLM or LoRA adapter state

boundaries: role multiplicity is not independent capacity
no natural language or multilingual transfer claim
fresh worlds remain sealed unless all development gates pass
